title: STEM Defocus Influenced Misinterpretations in Imaging Exciton Confinements
content: Stacking transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers with a relative twist or different lattice parameters produces moiré superlattices hosting interesting correlated phenomena [1]. Bound electron-hole pairs, or excitons, are localized in these material systems [2]. Optical spectroscopy at cryogenic temperatures is usually employed to study excitons but does not offer the nanometer-scale spatial resolution required to understand their localization [3]. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) coupled with low-loss electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) at cryogenic temperatures provides a way to study this excitonic confinement, offering superior 1 Å spatial and 10 meV spectral resolution. However, there are some complexities associated with the experiment, along with experimental instabilities, that need to be understood to ensure a valid interpretation of the data.
